subject.title: Feature: config-level default task notify policy

question: Should OpenClaw add a public task notify default config surface, and should that surface be global or per-runtime/channel-scoped?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding config/default behavior is a public product contract with channel-delivery and upgrade implications that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Add per-runtime defaults
options.body: Introduce an `agents.defaults.tasks` policy map, preserve current behavior when unset, and apply it before ACP, subagent, and Task Flow records are created.

options.title: Add one global default
options.body: Expose a single default notify policy for all task-like records while explicitly exempting cron, CLI, and media tasks that already have silent contracts.

options.title: Keep CLI-only overrides
options.body: Leave the current per-task `openclaw tasks notify` override as the supported path and close or redirect broader default-policy requests.

recommendation.title: Add per-runtime defaults
recommendation.body: Introduce an `agents.defaults.tasks` policy map, preserve current behavior when unset, and apply it before ACP, subagent, and Task Flow records are created.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the strongest recent history match for the task registry, ACP/subagent creation paths, config defaults, and release-tagged behavior involved in this decision.
